stem: Which feature best distinguishes the innate immune response from the adaptive immune response?

options.text: It retains memory of previously encountered pathogens
It uses physical barriers and non-specific phagocytic cells
It uses B and T cells to target specific antigens
It develops several days to weeks after first exposure
It produces antigen-specific antibodies after class switching

explanation: The innate immune response uses physical barriers and non-specific phagocytic cells as an immediate first-line defence.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because immune memory is a feature of the adaptive immune system, not the innate immune response.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because the innate immune response is the first line of defence and includes physical barriers such as skin and mucosa, as well as non-specific phagocytic cells.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because B and T lymphocytes are components of the adaptive immune response.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the innate immune response is immediate, whereas the adaptive response develops more slowly after first exposure.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because antigen-specific antibody production is a function of the adaptive immune response.

source.hint: Think about which part of the immune system acts as a generalized 'first responder' without learning from the past.
